newsitem.title: UKRAINE: EBRD says Ukraine could get total $500 mln in 1997.
newsitem.headline: EBRD says Ukraine could get total $500 mln in 1997.

text.p: Credits from the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) to Ukraine are expected to increase to $500 million in 1997 from $195 million this year, the director for Ukraine said.

"In keeping with Ukraine's economic reform programme and creation of a comfortable investment climate, we could finance projects up to $500 million," Yuri Poluneev said at a news conference on Thursday.
He said about 80 projects were ready for review.

The EBRD has been serving as the agency financing the closure of the Chernobyl nuclear power plant, whose fourth reactor exploded 10 years ago and sent a radiation cloud over Ukraine, Russia, Belarus and much of Europe.

Poluneev said the EBRD is providing $1.3 billion to finance construction of two nuclear reactors to replace energy which will be lost when Chernobyl closes. Ukraine has promised G7 countries it will shut the plant by 2000.
Other EBRD-financed projects include modernisation of Kiev hotels and construction of a new runway at Kiev's Borispil airport.
"The bank's priorities in Ukraine are the energy sector, development of the financial sector, the communications sector, privatisation, and food packaging in the agriculture sector," Poluneev said.
